purpose: This medicine helps your body make more red blood cells. It is used to treat anemia (low red blood cell count) caused by chronic kidney disease, chemotherapy, or certain other conditions. It can reduce your need for blood transfusions.
how_it_works: Your kidneys normally make a natural protein called erythropoietin that tells your bone marrow to produce red blood cells. This medication works just like that natural protein, signaling your bone marrow to make more red blood cells. More red blood cells mean more oxygen gets carried through your body, which helps you feel less tired and weak.
common_side_effects: High blood pressure, headache, joint or muscle aches, nausea, vomiting, fever, swelling in your legs or arms, and redness or soreness at the injection site are the most common side effects.
warnings: This medication can raise your risk of serious problems like blood clots, stroke, heart attack, and even death, especially if your red blood cell levels get too high. It may cause tumors to grow faster in some cancer patients. Tell your doctor right away if you have chest pain, trouble breathing, sudden numbness, or signs of a blood clot like leg swelling or pain. Never shake the vial, and do not use it if it contains particles or looks discolored.
typical_dosing: This medicine is given as an injection under the skin or into a vein, usually by a healthcare provider or nurse. The dose and how often you receive it depends on your condition, weight, and lab results. Your doctor will adjust your dose based on regular blood tests to keep your red blood cell levels in a safe range.
